collection.description: A villager is sitting in the sun.

ask.text:
(subject)'s grandchild, (child), has been learning spells from the old storyteller, little ones, mostly harmless: a song that makes flowers open, a rhyme to find lost things. Today (child) has learned a bigger one, about "giving back time," and is very excited, and wants to try it on (subject), because (subject) is the oldest person (subject.he/she) loves.
(subject) is sitting in the sun. (child) is standing in front of (subject.him/her) with a handful of dried flowers and a very serious face, already starting to chant. The storyteller, passing by, stops dead and looks worried.
Should (subject) let (child) finish the spell?

c1o1.text: The flowers sink into (subject)'s hair, and when (subject.he/she) opens (subject.his/her) eyes, the world looks sharper, and (subject.his/her) hands are strong and smooth, and (subject.his/her) hair is thick. Twenty years, gone. (child) jumps up and down. The storyteller sits down heavily and says (subject.he/she) is never teaching that one again. (subject) picks (child) up and swings (subject.him/her) round, which (subject.he/she) hasn't been able to do in years.

c1o2.text: The spell is strong, and (child) is very determined. When (subject) opens (subject.his/her) eyes, (subject.he/she) is twenty-five, and (subject.his/her) grandchild is looking at (subject.him/her) as if (subject.he/she) has done something terribly clever and terribly wrong at the same time. (subject) laughs until (subject.he/she) cries. "You'll still have to call me Grand(subject.father/mother)," (subject.he/she) says. "No matter how odd it looks."

c1.text: (subject) closes (subject.his/her) eyes and lets the chanting wash over (subject.him/her). (child) scatters the dried flowers over (subject.his/her) head. They smell of summer, and they don't fall to the ground. They hang in the air, glowing...

c2o1.text: Half a spell, it turns out, is still something. (subject)'s face has gone smooth and bright, as it was long ago, though the rest of (subject.him/her) is as old as ever. (child) is delighted with half a success. The storyteller makes (child) promise to only ever do whole spells, or none.

c2o2.text: (child) explains the spell, all of it, and (subject) listens to every word, and asks good questions. By the end (child) understands it much better than (subject.he/she) did, including all the ways it could have gone wrong. The storyteller takes (subject.him/her) on properly after that, and (child) gets very good at the little spells.

c2.text: (subject) takes (child)'s hands, very gently, and the chanting stops. "Not today," (subject.he/she) says. "I like being old. Tell me what the spell does instead..."
